stories.title: JLL Arranges Refi for Maine Self-Storage Asset
stories.excerpt: JLL has arranged a refinancing for a recently built self-storage facility managed by Extra Space Storage Inc. in South Portland, ME. Working on behalf of the borrower, The Ardent Companies, a JLL Capital Markets Debt Advisory team secured the five-year loan through a regional bank. Located at 193 Western Ave., just south of Portland International Jetport, Extra Space South Portland was completed in 2022 and has maintained high occupancy for 12 consecutive months. The 90,000-square-foot property features climate-controlled units with 24/7 access and serves a trade area of more than 125,000 households within a 30-minute drive. JLL noted that average household incomes exceed $1330,000 in the surrounding area, adding to the favorable conditions for the stabilized asset in one New England’s strongest self-storage markets. The post JLL Arranges Refi for Maine Self-Storage Asset appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Extra Space Storage, South Portland ME, refi on 90K-SF stabilized facility completed 2022.
Trade area 125K+ households, avg income $133K+, 12 months consecutive high occupancy.
Self-storage strength in New England signals broader demographic/economic resilience in Portland metro.
stories.summary: JLL arranged a five-year refinancing through a regional bank for a 90,000-square-foot climate-controlled self-storage facility in South Portland, Maine, completed in 2022 by Extra Space Storage. The property has maintained high occupancy for 12 consecutive months and serves a trade area of 125,000+ households with average incomes exceeding $133,000. The strong fundamentals underscore favorable market conditions in one of New England's strongest self-storage markets.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. Self-storage strength suggests robust household formation and income stability in Portland metro, which could signal underlying demand for rental apartments, but this is ancillary. No material supply, capital, or cost signals for apartment developers.

stories.title: BXP Acquires Boston-Area Office Buildings for $30M
stories.excerpt: Boston-based real estate investment trust BXP has acquired a pair of office buildings in Waltham, MA for a total of $30 million following a rezoning of the area. The REIT paid $17 million for 860 Winter St. and $13 million for 870 Winter St., according to county deed records cited by Banker & Tradesman. The properties are located within the Bay Colony office park, west of Boston. The seller was an affiliate of the Massachusetts Medical Society, an industry group that is based in 860 Winter St. The other building was previously occupied by defense contractor Raytheon. The Waltham City Council recently approved rezoning for multifamily development in the area, amid increasing efforts in Massachusetts to convert underutilized or vacant office buildings into apartments. BXP’s suburban Boston portfolio spans nearly 4 million square feet, including 16 properties in Waltham. The company broke ground on a 312-unit apartment complex in a Lexington, MA office park last year. The post BXP Acquires Boston-Area Office Buildings for $30M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: BXP acquires 860 & 870 Winter St, Waltham MA for $30M after city rezoning to multifamily.
Waltham rezoning enables office-to-residential conversion in Massachusetts' effort to repurpose vacant office.
BXP actively pivoting suburban Boston office portfolio to apartments; broke ground 312-unit Lexington last year.
stories.summary: Boston Properties acquired two office buildings in Waltham, Massachusetts for $30 million (860 Winter Street for $17M, 870 Winter Street for $13M) following a city rezoning that permits multifamily development. The buildings, previously occupied by the Massachusetts Medical Society and Raytheon, are located in Bay Colony office park west of Boston. BXP has a 4-million-square-foot suburban Boston portfolio spanning 16 Waltham properties and has already begun converting office parks to residential (312-unit Lexington complex).
stories.impact: BXP's aggressive office-to-residential pivot in greater Boston signals institutional capital recognizing structural office decline and multifamily opportunity in suburban markets. Waltham rezoning removes entitlement risk for conversion projects, lowering development costs and timelines. This creates competitive pressure for independent developers and signals sustained appetite for rezoned office sites in Boston suburbs—watch for similar conversions in nearby submarkets (Lexington, Cambridge, Burlington) as BXP and others build pipeline ahead of supply.

stories.title: Chicago/Midwest People & Company News, week of September 4, 2026
stories.excerpt: CBRE has promoted Chris Schastok to vice chairman, the firm’s highest professional title for producers. Schastok is a member of CBRE’s Site Selection & Incentives group within the Advisory Services Practice, based in Chicago. For more than 13 years at the firm, he has helped clients translate business objectives into site selection strategy and economic incentive negotiations, working alongside the broader planning and execution of corporate real estate initiatives. He has negotiated billions in incentives on clients’ behalf, with experience across corporate headquarters, food production, manufacturing and distribution center projects. Oxford Companies, a commercial real estate firm serving the greater Ann Arbor area, announced that Neal Warling has joined the company as director of sales and leasing. Warling will help lead Oxford’s brokerage activities, working with property owners, investors, tenants and corporate clients. The firm also announced the promotions of three longtime members of its leadership team, naming Joe Mifsud chief operating officer, Katie Vohwinkle senior vice president of operations, and Mike Van Patten senior vice president of asset management. PREMIER Design + Build Group announced that David Lewis has joined the company as general superintendent, based in its Columbus, Ohio, office. In his new role, Lewis will provide field leadership for the company’s Ohio operations, overseeing project execution while supporting operational excellence, safety, quality, and the continued development of field teams. Lewis brings more than four decades of construction experience, including more than 30 years in field management and leadership roles. CenterPoint Properties has appointed Ross Straseske as executive vice president and chief financial officer. bullets: CBRE Chicago promotes Chris Schastok to vice chairman; negotiated billions in incentives, HQ/industrial focus.
Oxford Companies Ann Arbor adds director of sales/leasing; leadership restructuring amid market activity.
PREMIER Design+Build Ohio hires general superintendent with 40+ years construction; field expansion signal.
stories.summary: This personnel roundup includes CBRE Chicago promoting Chris Schastok (vice chairman, site selection & incentives) after 13+ years negotiating billions in economic incentives for corporate HQ, manufacturing, and distribution projects; Oxford Companies (Ann Arbor) hiring a director of sales/leasing and promoting three ops/asset management leaders; and PREMIER Design+Build (Columbus) adding a general superintendent with 40+ years of field experience. No major capital, market, or regulatory news.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development demand, supply, capital, or cost. Personnel changes suggest steady corporate real estate and industrial activity in Chicago, Ann Arbor, and Columbus, but no specific signals on apartment market dynamics or development feasibility. Schastok's incentive expertise may indicate competitive site-selection activity that could favor industrial over multifamily in some Midwest corridors.

stories.title: CEDARst Snags $80M Construction Loan for San Diego Apartments
stories.excerpt: CEDARst obtained an $80 million construction financing for The Samuel, a 197-unit Class A multifamily development in San Diego’s North Park neighborhood. JLL worked on behalf of the CEDARst Companies, in arranging the three-year, floating-rate loan through CrossHarbor Capital Partners. The Samuel will be located at 2821 Adams Ave. in North Park. The eight-story development will feature 82 studios, 93 one- and 22 two-bedroom units, averaging 621 square feet, with 189 parking spaces. The development will include amenities such as a pool, fitness center, co-working lounge, fire pits, game deck and a rooftop sunset lounge with an outdoor kitchen. Construction is expected to begin in Q3 2026, with completion anticipated in Q4 2028. JLL Capital Market’s Debt Advisory team was led by Senior Director Zach Kersten, Director Jack Wood and Analyst Ben Choromanski. The post CEDARst Snags $80M Construction Loan for San Diego Apartments appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CEDARst secures $80M floating-rate construction loan, CrossHarbor Capital, for 197-unit San Diego North Park.
The Samuel: 8-story, 621 SF avg, studios/1-2BR mix, Q3 2026 start, Q4 2028 completion.
Class A amenity-heavy product (pool, fitness, co-work, rooftop lounge) in San Diego's gentrifying North Park.
stories.summary: CEDARst Companies obtained an $80 million three-year floating-rate construction loan through CrossHarbor Capital Partners for The Samuel, a 197-unit Class A multifamily development in San Diego's North Park neighborhood. The eight-story property at 2821 Adams Avenue will feature 82 studios, 93 one-bedroom, and 22 two-bedroom units averaging 621 square feet, with 189 parking spaces and premium amenities. Construction begins Q3 2026, with delivery expected Q4 2028.
stories.impact: Floating-rate construction financing in mid-2026 reflects ongoing capital availability for Class A apartment development despite higher rates; CEDARst's North Park site selection signals continued supply/demand tightness in San Diego infill submarkets. Q4 2028 delivery timing creates window for competitive market capture—monitor lease-up trajectory post-delivery and absorption of comparable Class A supply (Mission Valley, Pacific Beach) in San Diego. North Park gentrification momentum (rising rents, walkability, dining/retail) supports premium positioning and rent growth potential.

stories.title: Colliers Completes 67K-SF Industrial Lease in Maryland
stories.excerpt: Colliers completed a 67,040-square-foot industrial lease at 4780 Winchester Boulevard in Frederick, Maryland. Executive Vice Presidents Thomas Gentner, Brian Siegel and Jason Sullivan represented the landlord in the transaction. Link Logistics is an owner and operator of last-mile industrial real estate, with approximately 500 million square feet of warehouse space across 3,000 properties in North America. The new tenant, Senneca Holdings, Inc., is a manufacturer of data center containment solutions, specialty doors, and space separation systems. said Michael Walsh, Senior Vice President and Market Officer at Link Logistics. “We’re pleased to welcome Senneca Holdings and remain committed to providing properties that help our customers operate efficiently while meeting their evolving needs.” Located within one of the Mid-Atlantic’s most strategically positioned industrial corridors, 4780 Winchester Boulevard offers immediate access to Route 15, Interstate 70 and Interstate 270, providing connectivity to Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Northern Virginia and major East Coast population centers. bullets: Link Logistics leases 67K-SF to Senneca Holdings (data center containment solutions) Frederick MD.
4780 Winchester Boulevard: I-70/I-270/Route 15 access to DC/Baltimore/NoVa; strategic mid-Atlantic logistics hub.

stories.summary: Link Logistics completed a 67,040-square-foot industrial lease at 4780 Winchester Boulevard in Frederick, Maryland to Senneca Holdings, a manufacturer of data center containment solutions and specialty doors. The property offers direct access to Route 15, Interstate 70, and Interstate 270, positioning it at the nexus of Washington D.C., Baltimore, Northern Virginia, and major East Coast population centers.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Data center supplier tenant signals regional growth in computing infrastructure demand supporting tech/cloud expansion in DC-Baltimore corridor, which could drive secondary job growth and population inflow into multifamily-friendly submarkets. Frederick's logistics strength and I-70/I-270 connectivity may attract corporate relocations, but this is speculative. No immediate signal on apartment supply, financing, or construction costs.

stories.title: Reuben Brothers’ Jordana Yechiel On the Firm’s Big Bet on Century City
stories.excerpt: Century City has long been one of Los Angeles’ most concentrated office districts, but Reuben Brothers is betting that the area’s next chapter will look far more residential, experiential and luxury-driven. At Century Plaza, the development firm is building up around the Fairmont Century Plaza hotel and Park Elm condominiums, layering in restaurants, galleries, expansive wellness offerings and a revamped public plaza. For Jordana Yechiel (nee Reuben) of Reuben Brothers, the strategy reflects a larger shift in how people want to live in Los Angeles, drawing inspiration from Dubai’s International Financial Centre becoming a round-the-clock destination, where restaurants, culture and residences transformed what had largely been a business district. Commercial Observer spoke with Yechiel in late August about why Reuben Brothers made such a large bet on Century City, what luxury buyers expect, and how the firm is curating tenants rather than chasing occupancy and rent. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Reuben Brothers has traditionally focused on trophy real estate and hospitality. What made Century City and this project fit the portfolio? Jordana Yechiel: At Reuben Brothers, the anomaly in our portfolio is Century City. We started as a traditional real estate company, and then we went into hospitality and luxury hotels and some residential development. But these were always trophy assets, whether they were in London, or the Surrey Hotel on the Upper East Side, or we’ve now made the Waldorf Astoria out of the W in South Beach. Real trophy property first, hospitality second. So we look at the property as a property deal, because that’s the way our brains are wired, and then we bring the luxury to it. This is a new development. We’ve poured more money into this than anything else. Our belief behind this was we don’t want to just put more stuff out into the world. We want to say, “What’s missing? What’s working? How can we help?
bullets: Reuben Brothers betting Century City LA shifts from office-centric to residential/experiential/luxury mixed-use.
Park Elm Residences + Fairmont Century Plaza anchoring redevelopment; galleries, wellness, public plaza.
Strategy mirrors Dubai IFC model: 24/7 destination blending office, residential, dining, culture to attract affluent residents.
stories.summary: Reuben Brothers is executing a major repositioning of Century City, Los Angeles, layering residential (Park Elm Residences), hospitality (Fairmont Century Plaza expansion), restaurants, galleries, wellness, and public plaza improvements around what has long been a concentrated office district. Leadership cites inspiration from Dubai's International Financial Centre, which transformed a business hub into a round-the-clock mixed-use destination attracting affluent residents.
stories.impact: Century City's pivot from office to residential-experiential signals institutional recognition that LA's traditional office corridors face structural headwinds; Reuben Brothers' luxury-focused, mixed-use conversion approach (not pure apartment commodity play) targets high-income demand in high-barrier markets. This strategy may constrain multifamily-only competitive supply in Century City submarket while raising land/entitlement costs. Developers competing in Century City or similar LA office-to-mixed-use corridors (Playa Vista, Koreatown) must plan for amenity/retail intensity and higher hard/soft costs vs. suburban greenfield.

stories.title: Downtown D.C. Office Conversion Secures $176M Loan, New Majority Partner
stories.excerpt: One of Washington, D.C.’s largest office-to-residential redevelopments has secured a new majority partner and $175.6 million in construction financing. A partnership of Stonebridge, the Bernstein Companies and Criterion Real Estate Capital sold a 72 percent stake in the conversion of 1990 K Street NW to an entity managed by MetLife Investment Management for $58.7 million, according to records reported by the Business Journals. Kennedy Wilson Capital led the financing along with U.S. Fire Insurance, North River Insurance, Odyssey Reinsurance and Allied World Assurance. Cushman & Wakefield’s D.C.-based capital markets and debt advisory team arranged the financing. The roughly $250 million redevelopment, which will be rebranded as 1999 Eye Street NW, will replace the former office building with a 14-story, 412,000-square-foot mixed-use property. Plans call for 340 market-rate apartments, 44 affordable units, 50 student housing units totaling 200 beds, along with 15,600 square feet of retail and 189 parking spaces. Bernstein bought the property for $55.8 million in 2001, and Stonebridge and Criterion joined the ownership group last year. The conversion is part of Mayor Muriel Bowser Housing in Downtown program, which provides a 20-year tax abatement for office-to-residential conversions or redevelopments. Demolition started in September 2025. The project is part of D.C.’s Housing in Downtown program, which offers a 20-year tax abatement for qualifying commercial-to-residential conversions and redevelopments. It is the second-largest project in the program’s pipeline, behind the planned conversion of the Universal Buildings on Connecticut Avenue into roughly 600 units. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: 1990 K Street NW DC: $175.6M construction financing, MetLife IM takes 72% stake for $58.7M.
412K-SF office conversion to 14-story mixed-use: 340 market-rate + 44 affordable units, 50 student housing.
Downtown DC housing development part of Mayor Bowser's Housing in Downtown program; ~$250M total project cost.
stories.summary: A major office-to-residential redevelopment at 1990 K Street NW in downtown Washington, D.C. secured $175.6 million in construction financing and a new majority partner (MetLife Investment Management acquired a 72 percent stake for $58.7 million). The roughly $250 million project will convert the former office building into a 14-story, 412,000-square-foot mixed-use property featuring 340 market-rate apartments, 44 affordable units, and 50 student housing units, rebranded as 1999 Eye Street NW. Financing was led by Kennedy Wilson Capital with additional support from multiple insurance and reinsurance entities.
stories.impact: MetLife IM's majority acquisition signals strong institutional appetite for DC downtown residential despite office headwinds; $175.6M construction financing in mid-2026 affirms capital availability for conversion plays in gateway markets. DC's Housing in Downtown program (Bowser initiative) reduces regulatory friction and may offer tax incentives (TIF/PILOT/abatement), lowering developer hurdle rates. Developers eyeing downtown DC office conversions should move quickly to secure sites and entitlements before land prices rise; competitive supply from BPG, Stonebridge, and Criterion will intensify, compressing spreads. Monitor 1999 Eye Street lease-up closely for market rent/absorption signals in downtown DC multifamily.

stories.title: Geoff Mason Promoted to U.S. Chief Operating Officer of Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield
stories.excerpt: Retail operator Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield (URW) has elevated a longtime executive to the role of chief operating officer for its U.S. business. URW promoted Geoff Mason from vice president of asset management and development to COO after a series of successful development launches in Chicago, New Jersey and Southern California, according to the mall giant. Mason will be stepping into the shoes of Dominic Lowe, who will leave the company after 18 years, according to Westfield. “Geoff is an exceptional leader who brings a deep understanding of our U.S. portfolio, strong relationships across the organization and a clear vision for the future of our centers,” URW CEO Vincent Rouget said in a statement. Mason worked for URW from 2007 to 2016 before spending two and a half years at Macerich. He then returned to URW as senior vice president of operating management in 2018, according to Mason’s LinkedIn profile. “Over the past eight years, I have seen firsthand the strength of URW’s U.S. portfolio and the Westfield brand,” Mason said in a statement, adding that he plans to improve assets to serve as flagship locations for retailers. Mason assumed the role of COO on Sept. 1, according to Westfield. The appointment seems to strengthen the mall operator’s resolve to remain in the U.S. market despite plans announced in 2022 to focus on European assets. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield (URW) promotes Geoff Mason to U.S. COO after development launches in Chicago, NJ, SoCal.
Mason replaces Dominic Lowe (18 years); COO succession tied to URW's mall modernization/redevelopment strategy.
URW portfolio shift: retail operator investing in mixed-use/residential at its properties nationwide.
stories.summary: Retail operator Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield promoted Geoff Mason from vice president of asset management and development to chief operating officer of its U.S. business, succeeding Dominic Lowe after 18 years. Mason's promotion follows successful development launches in Chicago, New Jersey, and Southern California, signaling URW's ongoing shift in asset strategy.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. URW's COO succession and Mason's development track record suggest continued mixed-use/residential integration into traditional mall properties (Westfield centers). This may accelerate conversion or demolition of underperforming retail real estate into apartments in markets like Chicago, New Jersey, and SoCal, creating competitive supply headwinds for independent developers but also signaling institutional exit from pure-play retail and opening of land for residential redevelopment.

stories.title: Sagehall Picks Up Chetrit Organization’s 428 Broadway for $47M
stories.excerpt: An entity linked to New York City-based private real estate investment firm Sagehall has purchased Chetrit Organization’s office building at 428 Broadway for $47 million, according to city records filed Thursday. Jason Levine, managing director at Sagehall, signed for the buyer entity, 428 Broadway Owner. The seller entities are a partnership between the Chetrit Organization, for which Michael Chetrit signed on behalf of two holding companies, and investor American Industrial, co-founded by Roget Lerner and Jean-Marc Donics, the latter of whom signed on behalf of entity AI SoHo Investors. Chetrit Group purchased the six-story property in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood in 2005 for $22.5 million. It became the property of the Chetrit Organization in the years following the family’s enterprise split in the mid-2000s. The building eventually ran into distress after its four-floor anchor tenant, WeWork, filed for bankruptcy in 2023. The coworking firm’s departure from 428 Broadway left the building 96 percent vacant. Its current level of occupancy is unclear. Lender LoanCore Capital Credit began foreclosure actions against 428 Broadway in 2024, alongside 1 Whitehall Street in the Financial District, claiming default on roughly $200 million worth of loans. The latter office building was sold earlier this year for $105 million to Nathan Berman’s Metro Loft and Idan Ofer’s Quantum Pacific Group for a planned residential conversion. The mortgage debt on 428 Broadway appears to have changed hands from LoanCore to an entity belonging to Chetrit Organization and Donics, C&AI Soho Holding, in late 2025. The entity took ownership of the property in a recent foreclosure auction, allowing the partners to facilitate a sale. Donic declined to comment on the recent sale, while spokespeople for Sagehall and Chetrit did not immediately respond to requests for comment. bullets: Sagehall acquires 428 Broadway SoHo from Chetrit Organization for $47M; property 96% vacant post-WeWork exit.
WeWork bankruptcy 2023 left SoHo office distressed; Chetrit paid $22.5M in 2005, now down-sold.
Sagehall purchase signals opportunistic acquisition of office distress, likely targeting conversion or repositioning.
stories.summary: New York City-based investment firm Sagehall purchased Chetrit Organization's six-story office building at 428 Broadway in SoHo for $47 million. The property was acquired by Chetrit in 2005 for $22.5 million but fell into distress after its anchor tenant, WeWork, filed for bankruptcy in 2023 and vacated four floors, leaving the building 96 percent vacant.
stories.impact: SoHo office-to-residential conversion is plausible given Manhattan's office crisis, but Sagehall's acquisition strategy is unclear from the story. If conversion is the plan, this signals capital targeting SoHo infill multifamily supply opportunities; if repositioning to office/flex, the market thesis may be recovery. Developers should monitor 428 Broadway's redevelopment plans—SoHo's high land values, walkability, and cultural cachet make apartment conversion attractive despite zoning/entitlement risk. Comparable SoHo office conversions (if any execute successfully) will set comps and validate pricing for future residential projects in downtown Manhattan.

stories.title: Rockpoint Buys Oceanfront Fort Lauderdale Hotel for $47M
stories.excerpt: Rockpoint and Newbond Holdings have paid $47.1 million for an oceanfront resort in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., property records show. Called Hotel Maren Fort Lauderdale Beach, the property features 141 rooms at 525 South Fort Lauderdale Beach Boulevard, adjacent to Seebreeze Boulevard, south of Las Olas Boulevard. Magna Hospitality Group sold the 245,081-square-foot hotel, which is part of Hilton’s Curio Collection. “Hotel Maren is a high-quality beachfront property in a compelling submarket with attractive long-term fundamentals,” Patrick Ryan, a managing director at Rockpoint, said in a statement. “We believe there is a meaningful opportunity to build on the hotel’s existing strengths through targeted enhancements of the property and guest experience.” Apollo Global Management’s Athene Annuity & Life Assurance Company supplied a $47.7 million acquisition loan. A public deed listed the purchase price as $47.1 million, which likely valued only the hotel’s real estate. The final transaction value is probably higher to factor in the hotel’s business operations. A representative for Rockpoint declined to comment. The seller, Magna Hospitality, purchased the hotel out of bankruptcy mid-construction in 2018, paying $39.1 million, The Real Deal reported. Three years later, the Rhode Island-based hospitality company completed the 12-story building on a 0.7-acre site. The Rockpoint sale comes less than a month after El-Ad National Properties paid $60 million for another oceanfront hotel in Fort Lauderdale: the 1.2-acre, 99-room Sea Club Resort. Rockpoint, a private equity firm, has long been a major player in South Florida real estate. This year, the Boston-based firm has nabbed two construction loans each worth more than $100 million to build multifamily projects in Boca Raton and Palm Beach Gardens. It’s also a backer of Related Group and Two Roads Development’s luxury, oceanfront condo project in Bal Harbour, which obtained a $424 million construct
bullets: Rockpoint + Newbond Holdings acquire Hotel Maren Fort Lauderdale Beach for $47.1M, Curio Collection brand.
141-room beachfront property (245K SF) at 525 South Fort Lauderdale Beach Boulevard; Athene annuity financing.
Hospitality acquisition signals capital confidence in South Florida resort/leisure market; no apartment signal.
stories.summary: Rockpoint and Newbond Holdings purchased Hotel Maren Fort Lauderdale Beach, a 141-room oceanfront resort and part of Hilton's Curio Collection, for $47.1 million. Located at 525 South Fort Lauderdale Beach Boulevard, the 245,081-square-foot property was financed through a $47.7 million acquisition loan from Apollo Global Management's Athene Annuity & Life Assurance Company. Rockpoint cited attractive long-term submarket fundamentals and plans targeted enhancements.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Hospitality acquisition in Fort Lauderdale signals capital confidence in South Florida leisure/resort demand, which may correlate with broader population in-migration and job growth supporting apartment demand. However, no direct signal on residential supply, rents, or development feasibility. Hotel conversions to multifamily are rare in leisure-dependent submarkets like Fort Lauderdale Beach; monitor for any future residential redevelopment announcements on nearby oceanfront sites.
